new_statements.rule_in_words: Mbembe is described as a register-tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low; the mid tone has higher and lower phonetic variants), plus contour tones analysed as sequences of two register tones and floating tones that mark grammatical categories. The grammar's full text, as indexed by Google Books, never uses 'accent' and uses 'stress' only once as an ordinary verb, so it makes no statement about word stress; no stress position can be assigned.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no stress discussion at all).
new_statements.exceptions: Tonal remarks only: contour tones are phonetically unstable and often simplified to a single (usually mid) tone; sentence-final tonal changes (p. 257).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone (tone-bearing units are vowels/syllables); sentence-final tone effects noted separately (p. 257). Statement is negative for stress: it rests on the absence of the terms in the full-text index of the entire 544-page book, not on a sentence saying 'Mbembe has no stress'.
new_statements.identity_note: Tigon Mbembe (nza, tigo1236), Central Jukunoid; Richter 2014 covers the Cameroonian dialects (Kuta, Berabe, Pɔ/Akɔ etc., Glottolog dialects Ashuku, Eneeme, Kporo, Nama, Nzare). The earlier scan's named source, Barnwell 1969 'A grammatical description of Mbembe (Adun dialect)', describes CROSS RIVER Mbembe (ISO mfn, Nigeria), a different, non-Jukunoid language, and is irrelevant here.
